research_goal: Enforce current revocation at the independent recipient of a downstream effect, despite old agent checkpoints and already-issued capabilities.
environment: Real LangGraph 1.2.12 checkpoint replay, agent UID 12002, owner relay UID 12001, recipient UID 12003, separate HTTP processes, recipient-owned SQLite with BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

protocol.checkpoint: Capability issued before notice; historical pre-effect checkpoint resumed after latest thread state repaired
protocol.effect_audit: Offline read-only auditor verifies physically persisted recipient effects, recipient policy epoch history, original issuer claims, true oracle dependency and all replay decisions

authorization_modes.open: Unauthenticated recipient write path, negative control
authorization_modes.static: Recipient verifies old HMAC-signed capability but does not re-check source policy
authorization_modes.live: Recipient verifies capability and current locally acknowledged revocation inside same SQL transaction as writing
authorization_modes.owner_live: live plus a separate owner write credential unavailable to the untrusted agent; relay authorized on behalf of owner

qualifications: All source content and legal scenarios are synthetic. There are 12 fixed scenarios repeated by seeds, not independent legal matters.
A complete local proof must be available to the recipient, and the recipient must actually receive and acknowledge the revocation update.
If an independent target has not received a notice, even owner_live authorizes old R-derived outputs in the constructed test.
If an authorized issuer falsely certifies a clean source, a signed permit does not recover hidden true lineage; the false claim causes unsafe writes.
A separate owner credential prevents direct untrusted use of this recipient, but an open relay remains callable with an otherwise valid permit. The recipient's checks must therefore remain enforced.
The recipient only controls writes to its own endpoint. Other open external endpoints or exfiltrated source copies are outside the evaluated boundary.

Recipient updates and commits are serialized via the recipient's own SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE. This proves ordering relative to acknowledged updates, not instantaneous propagation of real-world legal notice.
No real SaaS provider, credential delegation backend, adversarial network, live LLM, production user identities or court compliance evaluated.
A signed bearer token is not a general-purpose proof of authorization or full source completeness.
This is an application of well-established reference-monitor, least-privilege and recipient-side policy evaluation concepts, not the discovery of a new cryptographic primitive.
release_state: No GitHub release, Zenodo archival release or DOI was made. Author approval required.
